A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched, including material moved into v3's Appendix A.3.

before.justification: v2 reports original learned optimal-transport maps and auction revenues in Section 7, Figures 2–3, and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains original transport-map and auction results in Section 6, Tables 1–3, Figure 1, and Appendix Figure 3.

M1.justification: The finite-support maximum parameterization, log-sum-exp smoothing, and single-level optimization framework are retained. v3 explicitly documents jointly trained supports and active-support allocation recovery, but presents these as implementation details of the existing model; the PDFs do not establish an underlying algorithm change.

E1.justification: The same transport problems and auction settings remain. However, Setting B changes its stated domain from [0,infinity)^n to [0,T]^n and its log-normal type distribution to a truncated distribution. v3 says truncation does not bind for the experimental samples, limiting the practical coverage difference.

E2.justification: Setting A retains Separate Posted Pricing and the same available SJA comparisons. Splitting its table removes only empty SJA cells for larger dimensions. Newly cited learned-auction papers are not evaluated as additional comparators, and Setting B still reports only the learned mechanism.

E3.justification: After matching the renamed outcome variable, Setting B's stated production cost changes from 0.1 times the Euclidean norm in v2 Section 7.2.2 to 0.1 times its square in v3 Section 6.3.2. This materially changes the seller's optimization objective. It is a reported setting revision; the unchanged revenues do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Section 6.1 adds a brief qualitative check of sensitivity to hard-max versus softmax evaluation, reporting nearly identical results at sufficiently high temperature. No quantitative temperature sweep or broader ablation is added. The existing transport and two-item auction visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Mean profit reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All tabulated revenues and empirical plot contents are retained, including Setting B's 1.022, 1.202, 1.250, and 1.253. v3 adds the qualitative finding that high-temperature softmax and hard-max evaluation give nearly identical results. Setting B's retained numbers accompany revised settings and therefore do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v3 adds subgradient and finite-difference reasoning and constructs an explicit generalized-convex kernel realizing the existing oscillatory counterexample. It adds a convex-Y assumption for the joint parameter-space claim, refines semiconvexity assumptions, and corrects the OT dual-improvement direction and displayed expected-profit formulation. The central density and gradient-approximation theorems and most appendix proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: universal approximation of generalized convex functions and gradients, a convex parameter space, and single-level formulations for transport and auctions. The abstract changes only theorem references; added future directions do not constitute new achieved contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes a convex parameter domain from nonconvex training, identifies Setting A as classical convexity, and explains that Setting B lacks twist and does not model complementarities. It also motivates controlled benchmarks with explicit kernels and identifies approximation rates and training convergence as future work. These substantively qualify the retained interpretations and applicability.

D1.justification: New Section 6.1 substantially expands implementation documentation: trainable supports and intercepts, finite-sample objectives, Adam/AdamW, constraint penalties, temperature annealing, hard-max evaluation, and allocation recovery without twist. The gconvex access information is retained. However, v2's hardware specification is removed, and numerical training settings and the truncation threshold remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dütting, two Curry papers, Ivanov, and Duan to position its retained auction dimensions against earlier learned-auction work. It removes Bronstein, Mirrlees, and Spence citations and narrows the architectural comparison to Maxout. Most related work remains unchanged; Gould's publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v3 places Method before Applications and replaces the standalone fully connected-layer comparison with a Maxout Analogy subsection. Background, gradient explanations, and experimental framing are extensively revised; type/outcome notation is standardized, implementation receives a dedicated subsection, and acknowledgments move to the end.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the architecture comparison around Maxout and moves it and the unchanged auction allocation plot to Appendix A.3. It splits v2's Setting A table into small- and large-dimension tables and revises table styling, typography, title formatting, and spacing throughout. The transport plot is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the retained contribution easier to assess through clearer mathematical assumptions, corrected formulations, implementation disclosures, and explicit applicability qualifications. These provide a supported overall gain. The improvement is limited by removed hardware information and unchanged Setting B revenues accompanying a materially revised cost and domain without explaining whether experiments were rerun.
